regressions.table_title: Job Polarization due to Quota Removals: All Textile Workers.
regressions.outcome_variable: MID^e_is (years of employment in mid-wage occupations of worker i in period s)

target_regressors.name: Import Competition
target_regressors.why: It is the difference-in-differences term Exposure99_ik x PostShock_s, the treatment of interest measuring rising Chinese import competition.

spec.sample_restrictions: All employees of the Danish textile and clothing sector in 1999 who are between 17 and 57 years old as of 1999 (N = 10,487 workers), each observed in a pre- and a post-period, giving N = 20,974 worker-period observations; 645 firm clusters.
spec.unit_of_observation: worker i x period s (pre-shock vs post-shock)
spec.outcome_construction: Number of years in period s that worker i's primary labor market position is employment in a mid-wage occupation. Mid-wage occupations are craft and related trade workers (ISCO 7), plant and machine operators and assemblers (ISCO 8), and clerks/office workers (ISCO 4), classified by 1999 median hourly wage in full-time jobs (Table 1).
data_construction_steps: Match MFA import quotas imposed on China to eight-digit Common Nomenclature (CN) goods.
Using firm-product level production data (VARES), identify firms producing quota-protected CN-8 goods in Denmark as of 1999.
Compute Exposure99_ik = sum over quota products p of Rev99_ikp / TotRev99_ik, the 1999 revenue share of quota goods of worker i's employer k.
Interact Exposure99_ik with Post_s (2002-2009 indicator) to form ImpComp_is.
Aggregate annual IDA worker data into pre- and post-shock periods (Bertrand, Duflo and Mullainathan, 2004) and count years in each labor market position.
spec.reproduction_notes: Estimation of Eq. (1) X_is = a0 + a1*Post_s*Exposure99_ik + a2*Post_s + delta_i + phi_is by OLS. Values in square brackets are the same regression re-estimated with a discrete treatment definition (revenue share larger than 0, Yes/No) instead of the continuous revenue share.

cells.row_label: Import Competition (discrete treatment definition, in square brackets)

evidence.snippet: Estimation of Eq. (1) using OLS. Dependent variables are given at the top of the columns.
Robust standard errors clustered at the level of the workers' initial firm (645 clusters) are reported in parentheses.
Results from employing a discrete treatment definition (revenue share larger than 0 Yes/No) are given in square brackets.

regressions.notes: The bracketed value is an alternative estimate from a separate regression using a binary treatment definition, printed within the same column.

regressions.table_title: Occupational Movements of Mid-wage Workers: The Role of Education.
regressions.outcome_variable: MID^e_is (years of employment in mid-wage occupations of worker i in period s)

target_regressors.name: ImpComp
target_regressors.why: The difference-in-differences coefficient alpha1 of Eq. (3), the average effect of import competition.

target_regressors.name: ImpComp × College
target_regressors.why: The triple-difference coefficient alpha3, giving the differential effect of import competition for college-educated workers; the paper's claim about education rests on it jointly with ImpComp.

controls: Post x College (college indicator interacted with time fixed effects)
spec.sample_restrictions: All 1999 textile and clothing workers who held mid-wage occupations as of the initial year 1999 (about 7000 workers); N = 13,934 worker-period observations in every regression.
spec.unit_of_observation: worker i x period s (pre-shock vs post-shock)
spec.outcome_construction: Number of years in period s that worker i's primary labor market position is employment in a mid-wage occupation (ISCO 4 clerks, ISCO 7 craft and related trade workers, ISCO 8 plant and machine operators and assemblers).
data_construction_steps: Compute Exposure99_ik as the 1999 revenue share of 8-digit CN goods of worker i's employer k that were subject to removal of quotas for China.
Define C_i = indicator for at least some college education as of 1999.
Estimate Eq. (3) X_is = a0 + a1*ImpComp_is + a2*Post_s + a3*ImpComp_is*C_i + a4*Post_s*C_i + delta_i + nu_is, adjusted for two instead of one initial characteristic.
Restrict to workers in mid-wage occupations in 1999 and aggregate annual data into pre- and post-shock periods.
spec.reproduction_notes: Estimates of alpha2 and alpha4 are not reported. Estimation of Eq. (3) adjusted for two instead of one initial characteristic, by OLS.

evidence.snippet: Estimation of Eq. (3) adjusted for two instead of one initial characteristic by OLS. Sample is all textile workers in mid-wage occupations as of the initial year 1999. The number of observations in every regression is N = 13,934.
Robust standard errors clustered at the firm level are reported in parentheses.

regressions.notes: The rows 'Worker FEs', 'Time FEs' and 'Educ. Indicators × Time FEs' are printed once under 'For all panels:' and apply to Panels A, B and C.
